title: Why a circle's area is πr²
summary: Cut a circle into slices and lay them side by side: they form an almost-rectangle πr wide and r tall.

beats.title: A circle of radius r
beats.narration: Here is a circle of radius r. Its rim, the circumference, is 2πr long.

beats.title: Cut it into slices
beats.narration: Cut it into 16 equal slices. The shaded half carries half the rim: πr of it.

check.question: Lay the slices side by side, tips alternating up and down. What shape appears?
check.explain: The slices interlock: the shaded arcs make the top edge, the others the bottom.

beats.title: Lay the slices in a row
beats.narration: Unroll the slices, alternating up and down. They interlock into an almost-rectangle.

beats.title: Measure its sides
beats.narration: Its top edge is half the rim, πr. Its height is a slice's length: r.

beats.title: Area = πr²
beats.narration: Width times height: πr × r. So a circle's area is πr².
